expectations.deliveries: every delivery, in order, checked exhaustively
expectations.exclusive: give one or the other; deliveries wins if both

note: Hand-authored expectations, not captured output. Replayed by tests/host/test_ble_fido_conformance.py (firmware C) and intended for crates/ble-framing (daemon Rust). A disagreement means one side is wrong on the wire.

vectors.name: single_fragment_message
vectors.why: An init fragment whose data length equals HLEN completes immediately.

vectors.name: empty_message
vectors.why: HLEN 0 completes on the init fragment. This is how CANCEL is sent.

vectors.name: cancel_from_idle
vectors.why: CANCEL is a zero-length message, not a special frame.

vectors.name: multi_fragment_message
vectors.why: 17 bytes in the init fragment, 19 per continuation at the 20-byte floor.

vectors.name: fragmentation_boundary_size_20
vectors.why: Fragment size is negotiated per connection; every legal size must work.

vectors.name: fragmentation_boundary_size_21
vectors.why: Fragment size is negotiated per connection; every legal size must work.

vectors.name: fragmentation_boundary_size_23
vectors.why: Fragment size is negotiated per connection; every legal size must work.

vectors.name: fragmentation_boundary_size_64
vectors.why: Fragment size is negotiated per connection; every legal size must work.

vectors.name: fragmentation_boundary_size_255
vectors.why: Fragment size is negotiated per connection; every legal size must work.

vectors.name: fragmentation_boundary_size_511
vectors.why: Fragment size is negotiated per connection; every legal size must work.

vectors.name: fragmentation_boundary_size_512
vectors.why: Fragment size is negotiated per connection; every legal size must work.

vectors.name: sequence_wraps_at_0x7f
vectors.why: SEQ is 7-bit and wraps 0x7f -> 0x00 rather than overflowing into the init bit. Unreachable against the firmware's 1200-byte ceiling, which is why it is pinned on the host side instead of being dropped.

vectors.name: sequence_cannot_wrap_within_the_device_ceiling
vectors.why: The largest message the device accepts, at the smallest legal fragment size, is 63 continuations. If this ever needs more than 0x7f, the wrap path becomes reachable on the device too and needs its own coverage.

vectors.name: max_length_message
vectors.why: CTAP_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE exactly; the largest the firmware will accept.

vectors.name: incomplete_message_yields_nothing
vectors.why: A partial transaction must not be delivered.

vectors.name: ping_payload_is_preserved
vectors.why: PING echoes its payload; the firmware answers it without the CTAP core.

vectors.name: empty_fragment
vectors.why: A zero-byte write carries neither a command nor a sequence number.

vectors.name: init_fragment_truncated_before_hlen
vectors.why: The 3-byte init header must be complete before HLEN can be read.

vectors.name: declared_length_above_ceiling
vectors.why: HLEN is 16-bit, so a peer can declare 65535. Reject before allocating.

vectors.name: declared_length_just_above_ceiling
vectors.why: The ceiling is inclusive; 1201 is one byte too many.

vectors.name: init_fragment_carries_more_than_declared
vectors.why: Data beyond HLEN in the init fragment is a length contradiction.

vectors.name: continuation_without_init
vectors.why: A continuation with no transaction in flight has nothing to continue.

vectors.name: first_continuation_must_be_seq_zero
vectors.why: Sequence numbers start at 0, not at 1.

vectors.name: skipped_sequence_number
vectors.why: A gap means a lost fragment; the message would be silently corrupt.

vectors.name: replayed_sequence_number
vectors.why: Replaying a fragment must not append it twice.

vectors.name: empty_continuation
vectors.why: A continuation with no data makes no progress, so a peer could hold the transaction open forever sending them.

vectors.name: continuations_exceed_declared_length
vectors.why: 17 + 19 overruns the declared 30; the buffer bound is HLEN, not the fragment.

vectors.name: fragment_longer_than_negotiated_size
vectors.why: fidoControlPointLength bounds *writes to fidoControlPoint*, so this rule is the device's alone. Inbound fragments reach the host as notifications on fidoStatus, sized by the negotiated ATT MTU, which may legitimately exceed it — a device advertising 20 and notifying at MTU-3 is conformant, so enforcing this host-side would be an interop bug.

vectors.name: init_fragment_mid_transaction
vectors.why: No channels exist, so an init mid-transaction is a protocol violation rather than a second conversation. Both implementations fail closed.

vectors.name: cancel_mid_transaction_abandons_and_stays_silent
vectors.why: CTAP2 11.4.8: 'Whether a request was cancelled or not, the authenticator MUST NOT reply to the cancel message itself.' So CANCEL is the one command permitted to interrupt a message in flight, and it emits nothing. Both implementations previously answered CMD_ERROR here, which is a MUST NOT violation neither of us caught by agreeing with the other.

vectors.name: cancel_with_a_payload_is_still_silent
vectors.why: Rejecting a malformed CANCEL would mean replying to it, which 11.4.8 forbids — the strict reading is unimplementable, not merely strict. The declared length is ignored and the payload discarded.

vectors.name: cancel_recovers_to_idle
vectors.why: Silence must not mean stuck: after a cancel the reassembler is idle and the next message goes straight through. The first vector to need `deliveries` — under a last-delivery-only rule an implementation that swallowed the CANCEL entirely would pass, and swallowing it is exactly the failure worth catching.

vectors.name: recovers_after_an_error
vectors.why: Failing closed must not wedge the transport: the abort leaves the reassembler idle, so the next well-formed init succeeds.

vectors.name: keepalive_written_to_control_point_is_rejected
vectors.why: KEEPALIVE is device-to-host only. The daemon's reassembler accepts it because it sits on the receiving end; the firmware must not.

vectors.name: error_written_to_control_point_is_rejected
vectors.why: ERROR is device-to-host only. The daemon's reassembler accepts it because it sits on the receiving end; the firmware must not.

vectors.name: unknown_command_0x80
vectors.why: Only the five defined commands exist; the high bit alone is not enough.
